executive_summary: Build failed with 100 compilation errors during test compilation phase. The primary root cause is a mismatch between test code expectations and actual DTO/service interface signatures. DTOs (TaskCreateRequest, TaskResponse, etc.) expect no-argument constructors but tests use parameterized constructors. Service methods expect different parameter types (String userId vs long, UUID taskId vs long). Additionally, ErrorResponse is missing getCode() method and GlobalExceptionHandler is missing handleValidationErrors() method.

errors.message: Constructor TaskCreateRequest cannot be applied to given types: required no arguments, found 5 parameters
errors.root_cause: TaskCreateRequest DTO class is defined with a no-argument constructor (likely using Lombok @NoArgsConstructor), but test code attempts to instantiate it with 5 parameters (title, description, userId, priority, dueDate). This pattern repeats across multiple test methods.
errors.fix_recommendation: Add @AllArgsConstructor to TaskCreateRequest DTO or use builder pattern (@Builder). Update DTO to: @Data @NoArgsConstructor @AllArgsConstructor public class TaskCreateRequest { ... }

errors.message: Constructor TaskResponse cannot be applied to given types: required no arguments, found 9 parameters
errors.root_cause: TaskResponse DTO class is defined with a no-argument constructor, but test code attempts to instantiate it with 9 parameters. Same issue as TaskCreateRequest.
errors.fix_recommendation: Add @AllArgsConstructor to TaskResponse DTO or use builder pattern. Update DTO to: @Data @NoArgsConstructor @AllArgsConstructor public class TaskResponse { ... }

errors.message: Method createTask in TaskService cannot be applied: required (String, TaskCreateRequest), found (TaskCreateRequest)
errors.root_cause: TaskService.createTask() method signature expects 2 parameters (String userId, TaskCreateRequest request), but test code calls it with only 1 parameter (TaskCreateRequest). This indicates the service interface was refactored to include userId parameter but tests were not updated.
errors.fix_recommendation: Update all createTask() mock calls in TaskControllerTest to include userId parameter: when(taskService.createTask(anyString(), any(TaskCreateRequest.class))).thenReturn(...)

errors.message: Method getUserTasks cannot be applied: required (String, int, int, String), found (long, int, int). Type mismatch: long cannot be converted to String
errors.root_cause: TaskService.getUserTasks() expects userId as String type with 4 parameters (userId, page, size, sortBy), but test code passes long type with only 3 parameters. The service interface was changed from long userId to String userId and added sortBy parameter.
errors.fix_recommendation: Update all getUserTasks() calls in tests to use String userId and include sortBy parameter: taskService.getUserTasks(String.valueOf(userId), page, size,

errors.message: Method getTaskById cannot be applied: required (UUID, String), found (long). Type mismatch: long cannot be converted to UUID
errors.root_cause: TaskService.getTaskById() expects UUID taskId and String userId parameters, but test code passes long taskId with no userId. The task ID type was changed from long to UUID and userId parameter was added.
errors.fix_recommendation: Update all getTaskById() calls to use UUID and include userId: taskService.getTaskById(UUID.fromString(taskId), userId). Update Task entity to use UUID as primary key type.

errors.message: Method updateTask cannot be applied: required (UUID, String, TaskUpdateRequest), found (long, TaskUpdateRequest)
errors.root_cause: TaskService.updateTask() expects 3 parameters (UUID taskId, String userId, TaskUpdateRequest), but test code provides 2 parameters (long taskId, TaskUpdateRequest). Similar to getTaskById issue.
errors.fix_recommendation: Update all updateTask() calls to use UUID taskId and include userId parameter: taskService.updateTask(UUID.fromString(taskId), userId, updateRequest)

errors.message: Cannot find symbol: method getCode() in ErrorResponse class
errors.root_cause: ErrorResponse DTO is missing getCode() method. Tests expect ErrorResponse to have a code field with getter, but the DTO class does not define this field.
errors.fix_recommendation: Add 'code' field to ErrorResponse DTO: @Data public class ErrorResponse { private String code; private String message; private LocalDateTime timestamp; }

errors.message: Type mismatch: Priority cannot be converted to TaskPriority
errors.root_cause: Test code uses Priority enum but InMemoryTaskDataStore expects TaskPriority enum. There are two different enum types for priority, causing type incompatibility.
errors.fix_recommendation: Standardize on one Priority enum type. Either rename TaskPriority to Priority or update all references to use TaskPriority consistently across the codebase.
